Making the Commute Less of a Grind

For a journey you make most days and have stopped thinking about. It decides what the time is for, buys back five minutes, keeps work email shut until you arrive, and marks the end of the trip so the day does not blur into it.

Commuting · Work · Habits · Stress · 9 items · once a day

The checklist

  • Pick one thing the journey is for — reading, music or nothing, but decide rather than drift.
  • Leave five minutes earlier than feels necessary — five minutes buys back the tone of the morning.
  • Keep work email shut until you arrive — answering on the move means arriving already behind.
  • Have one thing that marks the end of the journey — a coffee, a walk round the block, a changed shirt.
  • Download what you need the night before — hunting for signal is its own small misery.
  • Keep water and something to eat in the bag — hungry and stuck is a worse kind of stuck.
  • Work out what delay you can absorb and plan for it — a route with no slack fails every week.
  • Use the way home to put the day down — arriving with work still running costs you the evening.
  • Ask once a month whether this journey is worth it — a commute you never question quietly sets your life.

Use this checklist Free account: tick items off and keep each day's record.

How to use it

Run through it once a day, honestly and without scoring yourself. A checklist is a way of noticing, not a test: an item you cannot tick is information about the day, not a verdict on you. Over a few weeks the pattern of what gets ticked and what does not says more than any single pass.

With a free Theraglee account the checklist remembers each pass, so you can look back. Without one, you can still read it here and keep your own copy.
